# Langfuse OpenCode Plugin

> [!NOTE]
> This is `@mageyuki/opencode-observability-plugin`, an **unofficial fork** of
> [`@langfuse/opencode-observability-plugin`](https://github.com/langfuse/opencode-observability-plugin)
> that adds [prompt linking](#prompt-linking). It is not maintained or supported
> by Langfuse. Use `@mageyuki/opencode-observability-plugin@0.5.2-mageyuki.3` in
> place of `@langfuse/opencode-observability-plugin` in the examples below. See
> [FORK.md](./FORK.md) for the upstream base, the version scheme and the
> upstream status.

OpenCode plugin that sends OpenCode session telemetry to Langfuse. It traces user turns, assistant generations, tool calls, retries, reasoning output, compaction output, and failed generation steps.

## Quick Start

For OpenCode 2, enable the plugin in your configuration:

```json
{
  "plugins": ["@langfuse/opencode-observability-plugin@latest"]
}
```

For OpenCode 1, use the same package in your `opencode.json` or `opencode.jsonc`:

```json
{
  "plugin": ["@langfuse/opencode-observability-plugin@latest"]
}
```

Restart OpenCode after changing the config.

## Supported Versions

The default package entrypoint supports both OpenCode 1 and OpenCode 2. OpenCode
1 calls the plugin's `server()` implementation, while OpenCode 2 calls its
`setup()` implementation. The `/v1` and `/v2` entrypoints remain available for
direct imports.

Validated versions and entrypoints:

- OpenCode `2.0.4` and newer: `@langfuse/opencode-observability-plugin`
- OpenCode `1.18.29` and newer: `@langfuse/opencode-observability-plugin`

## Langfuse Credentials

Create `~/.config/opencode/opencode-langfuse.json` with your Langfuse credentials.

```json
{
  "publicKey": "pk-lf-...",
  "secretKey": "sk-lf-...",
  "baseUrl": "https://cloud.langfuse.com",
  "environment": "development",
  "userId": "your-user-id"
}
```

Only `publicKey` and `secretKey` are required. If `baseUrl` is not set, the plugin uses `https://cloud.langfuse.com`. If `environment` is not set, it uses `development`.

You can also set credentials with environment variables:

```bash
export LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY="pk-lf-..."
export LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY="sk-lf-..."
export LANGFUSE_BASE_URL="https://cloud.langfuse.com"
export LANGFUSE_ENVIRONMENT="development"
export LANGFUSE_USER_ID="your-user-id"
```

If both `LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY` and `LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY` are set, the plugin uses environment variables instead of reading the config file. Optional values can be supplied either way.

## Prompt Linking

The plugin can link each OpenCode 2 generation to the [Langfuse prompt](https://langfuse.com/docs/prompt-management/get-started) version that holds the agent's prompt. It is off unless you configure it with plugin options:

```jsonc
{
  "plugins": [
    {
      "package": "@langfuse/opencode-observability-plugin@latest",
      "options": {
        "promptLinking": {
          // Prompt name for each agent; {agent} is replaced by the agent name.
          "agentPrompt": "agents/{agent}",
          // Optional explicit names, preferred over agentPrompt. null skips an agent.
          "agents": { "build": null },
        },
      },
    },
  ],
}
```

How it works:

- The plugin reads the prompt versions from the Prompt Management API (`/api/public/v2/prompts`) with the configured Langfuse credentials, so the key needs read access to prompts. Bodies are fetched with `resolve=false` and only their hashes are kept in memory.
- A generation is linked only when one whole system part equals a version's text after converting CRLF to LF and trimming trailing whitespace. A part that merely contains or extends a version's text is not linked. When the version's `config.model` (`<providerID>/<modelID>`) or `config.variant` is set, it must match the generation as well. A missing key leaves the version unconstrained, but a key that is present with a value that is not a non-empty string of at most 256 characters (for example `null`, a number, an object or `""`) makes that version unlinkable. Among versions with identical text, model and variant the newest is linked; any other ambiguity leaves the generation unlinked.
- Chat prompts and prompts that reference other prompts (`@@@langfusePrompt:`) are not linked. A prompt whose versions are all unlinkable reports `unavailable`.
- Linked generations get `langfuse.observation.prompt.name` and `langfuse.observation.prompt.version`. Every judged generation also gets `promptLink` metadata with `name`, `status` (`matched`, `no_match`, `ambiguous`, `not_registered` or `unavailable`) and, when matched, `version`.
- Tracing never waits for the prompt API. Versions are cached for 60 seconds; while the API is failing or slow, generations are left unlinked with status `unavailable`.
- Refreshes are driven by generations, not timers. A generation that uses a prompt name starts a background refresh once its cached versions are older than 45 seconds, so the cache stays current while that agent keeps generating. The first generation after more than 60 seconds without one for that name finds no usable cache: it starts with a provisional `unavailable` and is judged once more when its step ends. After a failed refresh the name stays `unavailable` until a refresh completes; retries back off from 10 seconds to 10 minutes.
- The `promptLink` written when a step starts is replaced when the step ends or fails. A generation that OpenCode closes without a step end (for example when the session finishes first) keeps the value from its start, which can be the provisional `unavailable`.
- Limits: at most 200 versions per prompt name, at most 1 MiB of prompt text per version (decoded UTF-8) and at most 1 MiB + 64 KiB per serialized API response, at most 2 concurrent requests with a 3 second timeout, and at most 64 prompt names per OpenCode process. A prompt over the version or text limit is recorded as `unavailable` in a completed snapshot: its version list is still refreshed like any other, but it is not retried with failure backoff and oversized bodies are not fetched again. Names beyond the 64th are reported as `unavailable` without any request, and one warning is logged.
- Options are fixed for the OpenCode process by the first plugin instance. If a re-created instance has different options, prompt linking stays off until OpenCode restarts.
- Invalid `promptLinking` options log one warning per OpenCode process and disable only prompt linking.
- OpenCode 1 does not expose the system prompt to plugins, so prompt linking applies to OpenCode 2 only.

## Prompt Versions

The plugin can record which version of a global instruction file (`AGENTS.md`) and which agent prompt version each OpenCode 2 generation actually ran with, so scores can be grouped by version with the Langfuse Metrics API (`traceRelease`, `traceVersion`). It is off unless you configure it:

```jsonc
{
  "plugins": [
    {
      "package": "@mageyuki/opencode-observability-plugin@0.5.2-mageyuki.3",
      "options": {
        "promptLinking": { "agentPrompt": "agents/{agent}" },
        "promptVersions": {
          "instructions": {
            // The instruction file as OpenCode prints it in "Instructions from: <path>".
            "path": "~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md",
            // The Langfuse prompt that holds the versions of that file.
            "prompt": "policy/AGENTS",
          },
          "release": "instructions", // optional, the only accepted value
          "version": "agentPrompt", // optional, the only accepted value
        },
      },
    },
  ],
}
```

Options:

| Input                                                           | Handling                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| --------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `promptVersions` absent or `null`                               | Off; the spans are the same as without the feature.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Not an object (`true`, a string, an array) or `{}`              | Invalid.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Keys other than `instructions` (required), `release`, `version` | Invalid.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `instructions`                                                  | An object with exactly `path` and `prompt`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `path`                                                          | A non-empty absolute path, or one starting with `~/` (replaced by the home directory). `~` alone, `~user/`, relative paths and `$VAR` are invalid. Only normalized paths are accepted: a `.` or `..` segment, an empty segment (`//`) or a trailing `/` is invalid. Symlinks are not resolved. |
| `prompt`                                                        | 1 to 256 characters, without `{`, `}` or a newline. It must not be a name the same instance's `promptLinking` uses for agent prompts (an `agents` value, or a name the `agentPrompt` pattern matches).                                                                                         |
| `release`, `version`                                            | `"instructions"` and `"agentPrompt"` only (the defaults).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |

Invalid options log one warning (key names only) and disable only prompt versions; tracing and prompt linking continue. Options are fixed for the OpenCode process by the first plugin instance; a later instance with different (or missing, or invalid) `promptVersions` disables prompt versions until OpenCode restarts, without affecting prompt linking.

Values:

- `langfuse.release`: `policy/AGENTS@<N>` (the block equals version N), `policy/AGENTS#<sha12>` (an unregistered body, with the first 12 hex digits of its sha256), either followed by `+changed` when OpenCode reported that the file changed during the session, or `policy/AGENTS:mixed` when a turn or window holds more than one value. The prefix is the configured `prompt`.
- `langfuse.version`: `agents/<name>@<N>` when prompt linking matched, otherwise the agent name (for example `build`), or `mixed`.
- Metadata (`langfuse.observation.metadata.<key>`): `agentsMdVersion`, `agentsMdStatus` (`matched`, `no_match`, `absent`, `ambiguous`, `boundary_unknown`, `unavailable`, `mixed`), `agentsMdChanged`, `agentsMdSha12`, `agentPromptStatus` (`matched`, `not_registered`, `no_match`, `ambiguous`, `unavailable`, `disabled`, `mixed`), `otherInstructionCount` (other instruction blocks, counted only) and `promptVersionsSchema` (`1`). Every metadata value is written as a string (for example `"7"`, `"true"`), because the Langfuse SDK warns on export for non-string `langfuse.observation.metadata.*` attributes.
- Only names, version numbers, a 12-hex hash prefix, statuses, booleans and counts are written; never instruction text or paths. When the value is unknown, `langfuse.release` is left unset and only the status is recorded.

How it works and its limits:

- The block of the configured path is found in the system prompt by its `Instructions from: <path>` header and ends at the first blank line followed by another header or the `Today's date:` line (the OpenCode v2.1.1 format). Without that terminator the status is `boundary_unknown` and no release is written. Its text, with CRLF converted to LF and trailing whitespace trimmed, is hashed and compared with the newest 50 versions of the prompt; the newest version with exactly that text wins. Versions whose text contains a blank line followed by `Instructions from: ` or `Today's date: ` are not indexed.
- A change notice of OpenCode v2.1.1 for the configured path in the messages (`The instructions from <path> changed. Here's the diff:`, `… no longer apply.`, or `New instructions apply from:` followed by the path's block) marks the value `+changed`. If OpenCode changes these texts, changes are no longer detected and the session's starting version is recorded.
- A generation is stamped once, when its value is final (at step start, or at step end at the latest). A turn is stamped right before it ends from its generations. Every other span with a `session.id` (tools, events, evaluation tasks) is stamped when it starts from the values determined inside its window `[start, now]`, or, if there are none, the last value before it. A window that starts before the OpenCode process started, before history that had to be dropped, or while a generation of the session is still undetermined gets only `agentsMdStatus=unavailable`. So does a window with no value determined inside it or before it (for example a session first seen after OpenCode restarted, or after a reset of the plugin's whole state).
- The history is kept per session, so a subagent's generations do not count for its parent's spans. In the Metrics API a subagent turn's score is grouped by the trace root's (the parent's) values.
- These attributes are written after the Langfuse span processor, so a `LANGFUSE_RELEASE` environment variable does not override them; spans that get no release keep the environment value.
- The span processors are the same as without the feature. OpenCode 1 is not supported.

# Changelog

This changelog covers the unofficial `@mageyuki/opencode-observability-plugin`
fork. For upstream changes see the
[upstream releases](https://github.com/langfuse/opencode-observability-plugin/releases).

## 0.5.2-mageyuki.4

Based on upstream `v0.5.2` (`24389efd13decfb72e103950526669addcb245e8`).

### Fixed

- In an OpenCode 2 server with several locations (directories or
  worktrees), the disposal of an idle location ended the open turns,
  generations and tools of sessions at the other locations and cleared the
  prompt version history and parent session links of every session. Turns
  were cut off early, evaluation tasks lost their `langfuse.release`, and
  child sessions that continued later became root traces. A disposal now
  ends and forgets only the sessions its plugin instance holds, and keeps
  their version history and parent links. A late hook from a location that
  a session moved away from is still traced but no longer takes the session
  from the instance that holds it; run events of an instance while another
  instance holds the session, and hooks and run events after a disposal,
  are ignored.

### Changed

- With `promptVersions`, a window that has no value determined inside it or
  before it (for example a session first seen after a restart) is stamped
  `agentsMdStatus=unavailable` instead of getting no prompt version
  attributes. This includes spans of a new session before its first
  generation and turns without a determined generation; no release is
  written for them, as before. A reset of the plugin's whole state makes the
  windows that start before it `unavailable`.
- Dependency ranges are the same as `0.5.2-mageyuki.3`.

## 0.5.2-mageyuki.3

Based on upstream `v0.5.2` (`24389efd13decfb72e103950526669addcb245e8`).

### Fixed

- A fresh `npm install` of `0.5.2-mageyuki.1` or `.2` resolved
  `@langfuse/otel@5.14.0`, whose peer range `>=0.202.0 <1.0.0` admits
  `@opentelemetry/exporter-trace-otlp-http@0.300.0` and
  `@opentelemetry/otlp-exporter-base@0.300.0` (OpenTelemetry JS 3.x, which
  needs `@opentelemetry/api >=1.10.0 <1.11.0`). The plugin keeps
  `@opentelemetry/api` at 1.9.x with the 2.x SDK packages, so loading failed
  with `SyntaxError: ... '@opentelemetry/api' does not provide an export named
'SeverityNumber'`. The package now declares both exporter packages as direct
  dependencies with the range `>=0.202.0 <0.300.0` (still inside the
  `@langfuse/otel` peer range), so installs resolve the OpenTelemetry 2.x
  compatible line (`0.221.0` in the lockfile). No source change.
- `0.5.2-mageyuki.2` is deprecated for this reason; use
  `0.5.2-mageyuki.3` or later.

## 0.5.2-mageyuki.2

Based on upstream `v0.5.2` (`24389efd13decfb72e103950526669addcb245e8`).

### Added

- Opt-in prompt version attribution for OpenCode 2 through the
  `promptVersions` plugin option. Generations, turns and every other span of
  the same session get the `AGENTS.md` version that was actually loaded
  (`langfuse.release`, for example `policy/AGENTS@51`) and the agent prompt
  version (`langfuse.version`, for example `agents/reviewer@12`), plus status
  metadata. See [Prompt Versions](./README.md#prompt-versions).
- The instruction prompt (for example `policy/AGENTS`) is indexed from its
  newest 50 versions, without model/variant constraints, so it stays usable
  past 200 versions. Agent prompts keep the existing rules.

### Changed

- No new span processor: the existing app-root processor stamps the other
  spans of a session. Without `promptVersions` options the spans are the same
  as `0.5.2-mageyuki.1` apart from `langfuse.plugin.version`.

## 0.5.2-mageyuki.1

Based on upstream `v0.5.2` (`24389efd13decfb72e103950526669addcb245e8`).

### Added

- Opt-in prompt linking for OpenCode 2 through the `promptLinking` plugin
  option. A generation whose system part equals a Langfuse prompt version gets
  `langfuse.observation.prompt.name` and `langfuse.observation.prompt.version`,
  and judged generations get `promptLink` metadata. See
  [Prompt Linking](./README.md#prompt-linking).

### Changed

- Published as `@mageyuki/opencode-observability-plugin`. Without
  `promptLinking` options the spans are the same as upstream `v0.5.2` apart
  from `langfuse.plugin.version`.

# Fork notes

`@mageyuki/opencode-observability-plugin` is an unofficial fork of
[`@langfuse/opencode-observability-plugin`](https://github.com/langfuse/opencode-observability-plugin).
It is not maintained or supported by Langfuse. The upstream MIT license and
copyright notice in [LICENSE](./LICENSE) apply unchanged.

## Upstream base

- Upstream tag: `v0.5.2`
- Upstream commit: `24389efd13decfb72e103950526669addcb245e8`
- The lockfile is based on the upstream `v0.5.2` lockfile with this fork's
  added direct dependency declarations (resolved versions otherwise kept);
  build with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`.

## Changes from upstream

The fork keeps separate change sets on top of the upstream base:

1. **Prompt linking** (feature). Opt-in linking of OpenCode 2 generations to
   Langfuse Prompt Management versions through the `promptLinking` plugin
   option; see [Prompt Linking](./README.md#prompt-linking). It touches
   `src/prompt-link.ts`, `src/langfuse.ts`, `src/v2.ts`, the README section and
   the tests under `test/integration/`. This change set is kept free of fork
   identity so it can be ported to upstream on its own. The marker symbol that
   detects a shared client created by another build
   (`Symbol.for("langfuse.opencode.promptLinking.v1")`) exists only because the
   fork and upstream can share one process; an upstream port can drop it.
2. **Prompt versions** (feature, `0.5.2-mageyuki.2`). Opt-in attribution of
   the loaded `AGENTS.md` version and agent prompt version to
   `langfuse.release` / `langfuse.version` through the `promptVersions` plugin
   option; see [Prompt Versions](./README.md#prompt-versions). It adds
   `src/prompt-versions.ts` (option parsing, instruction scan, values and the
   single attribute writer) and `src/prompt-version-history.ts` (per-session
   history), adds the instruction prompt lookup and its owner rule to
   `src/prompt-link.ts`, wires the end paths and the existing app-root
   processor in `src/langfuse.ts`, and adds the README section and tests under
   `test/integration/`. It builds on the prompt linking change set and is not
   proposed upstream yet (the upstream proposal is tracked in
   `mageyuki/opencode-config#202`).
3. **OpenTelemetry dependency range** (fix, `0.5.2-mageyuki.3`).
   `@opentelemetry/exporter-trace-otlp-http` and
   `@opentelemetry/otlp-exporter-base` are direct dependencies constrained to
   `>=0.202.0 <0.300.0`. Upstream leaves them to the `@langfuse/otel` peer
   range `>=0.202.0 <1.0.0`, which lets a fresh install pick the
   OpenTelemetry JS 3.x line (`0.300.0`) that needs
   `@opentelemetry/api >=1.10.0` and fails to load next to the 2.x SDK
   packages. `0.5.2-mageyuki.1` and `.2` are affected; `.2` is deprecated. The
   `knip` config ignores `otlp-exporter-base`, which no source file imports.
   Drop the constraint only once `@langfuse/otel` supports the 3.x line and
   the plugin's own OpenTelemetry SDK/resources/api dependencies (currently
   `^2.x` / api `^1.9.1`) are migrated and verified compatible with the
   OpenTelemetry JS 3.x line.
4. **Package identity**. Package name, version, description and repository
   links, this file, [CHANGELOG.md](./CHANGELOG.md), the README notice and the
   package name used by the tests to import the built package.
5. **Location-scoped cleanup** (fix, `0.5.2-mageyuki.4`). OpenCode 2 runs one
   plugin instance per location (directory or worktree) and disposes an
   instance when its location has been idle, while all instances of the
   process share one client. Upstream's disposal ends every open observation
   and clears the whole trace state, including the prompt version history and
   the links of child sessions to their parents, so evicting one location cut
   off the open turns of sessions running at other locations and left their
   evaluation tasks without a release. Here the shared client records which
   instance holds each session (`src/session-holds.ts`): a hook is always
   traced and moves the hold to its instance when the instance is at the
   session's current location (recorded from `session.moved`), and only the
   holder applies run events. A session that nobody holds can be taken by any
   instance, so a move lost in a disposal cannot strand it; the instance at
   the recorded location takes it back at its first hook. A disposal ends
   and forgets only the sessions its instance holds and keeps their version
   history, parent link and location; `session.deleted` forgets everything
   of the session. A window with no recorded history is
   `agentsMdStatus=unavailable` instead of unstamped, and a reset of the whole
   state invalidates the windows that start before it. It touches `src/v2.ts`,
   `src/langfuse.ts`, `src/prompt-version-history.ts`, the README and the
   tests under `test/integration/`. The OpenCode 1 entry (`src/v1.ts`) is
   unchanged. Upstream has the same disposal behavior (as of `v0.6.0`); this
   fix is not proposed upstream. The marker symbol
   `Symbol.for("langfuse.opencode.sessionHolds.v1")` detects a shared client
   created by another build, which has no holds; the plugin then only
   flushes on disposal.

Without `promptLinking` and `promptVersions` options the plugin sends the same
spans as upstream `v0.5.2` in a process with one location; only the
`langfuse.plugin.version` attribute differs. With several locations, the
disposal of one location does not end the observations of sessions at other
locations, which upstream does (change set 5). The plugin id
(`langfuse.observability`), the tracer scope (`opencode-langfuse-plugin`), the
entrypoints (`.`, `./v1`, `./v2`) and the span processors are unchanged.

## Operational limits of prompt linking

These are accepted for this release; the README section
[Prompt Linking](./README.md#prompt-linking) is the user-facing description.

- **Demand-driven refresh.** No timers keep the cache warm. A generation that
  uses a prompt name refreshes it in the background once the cache is older
  than 45 seconds. After more than 60 seconds without a generation for that
  name, the next generation starts with a provisional `unavailable` and is
  judged once more at step end.
- **Provisional metadata.** The `promptLink` written at step start is replaced
  at step end or failure. A generation span closed without a step end (the
  plugin's `endActiveGenerationSteps`, for example when the session finishes
  first) keeps the start value, which can be `unavailable`.
- **Size limits.** At most 1 MiB of decoded prompt text (UTF-8 bytes) per
  version and at most 1 MiB + 64 KiB per serialized API response; at most 200
  versions per name. A prompt over these limits is recorded as `unavailable` in
  a completed snapshot, not treated as a failure, so it is not retried with
  backoff.
- **Bounds on retained state.** Only hashes of prompt text are kept. A
  `config.model` or `config.variant` that is present but not a non-empty string
  of at most 256 characters makes that version unlinkable instead of
  unconstrained. At most 64 prompt names are tracked per process, without
  eviction; later names report `unavailable` without requests and log one
  warning.
- **Warnings.** Invalid `promptLinking` options warn once per process. Fetch
  problems warn once per name and state change with an HTTP status or
  `transport failure` only.

## Version scheme

Versions are `<upstream version>-mageyuki.<N>`, starting at `N = 1` for each
upstream base (for example `0.5.2-mageyuki.1`). The plugin writes its package
version to `langfuse.plugin.version` on every span, so this keeps fork traces
distinguishable from upstream ones without claiming a future upstream version
number.

These are prerelease versions: publish them with an explicit dist-tag, for
example `npm publish <tarball> --access public --tag latest`. The release
workflow in `.github/workflows/` belongs to the upstream package and is not used
for fork releases.

## Following upstream

The fork does not follow upstream automatically. A newer upstream release is
adopted only after its output changes have been checked against the consumers
of these traces; the feature change set is then rebased onto that upstream tag
and released as `<upstream version>-mageyuki.1`.

## Upstream status

- Proposal: [langfuse discussion #18983](https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/18983).
- Upstream pull request: not opened yet.

If upstream ships an equivalent feature, consumers should move back to
`@langfuse/opencode-observability-plugin` and this fork stops publishing.
Published fork versions stay as they are.
